title: A scheme finite over a separated finite-type scheme
statement: Let $\nu:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism of schemes and $g:X\to S$ a morphism which is separated and of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then $g\circ\nu:Y\to S$ is separated and of finite type. In particular, if $X$ is a separated scheme of finite type over a field $k$, so is every scheme $Y$ with a finite morphism $Y\to X$ (with the composite structure morphism).

source.place: Morphisms, Section 29.44, Definition (definition-integral-finite): a finite morphism is affine with finite ring maps over affine opens; Morphisms Lemma 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated: affine morphisms are separated); affine morphisms are quasi-compact; finite ring maps are of finite type, so finite morphisms are locally of finite type (Morphisms Lemma 01WJ, lemma-finite-integral, with Algebra 00GK); Schemes Lemma 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence (1): composition of separated morphisms) and Morphisms Lemma 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type)
